## 3\. Local simplex preservation and strict positive-time positivity

The uniform ellipticity result gives local strong solvability for smooth simplex data, including data with pointwise zeros, by standard normally parabolic quasilinear theory.

There is also a componentwise positivity mechanism that works for every friction array.

Fix a species \(i\)\. In the region \(c_i\leq1/2\), define

\[
d_i(c)=\sum_{j\ne i}f_{ij}c_j
\geq\frac{f_-}{2}.
\]

Rearranging its Maxwell–Stefan flux equation,

\[
J_i=-\frac1{d_i(c)}\nabla c_i+c_iW_i,
\qquad
W_i=\frac1{d_i(c)}\sum_{j\ne i}f_{ij}J_j.
\]

Therefore, in this region,

\[
\boxed{
\partial_t c_i+(b+W_i)\cdot\nabla c_i
=\nabla\cdot\left(\frac1{d_i(c)}\nabla c_i\right)
-c_i\nabla\cdot W_i.
}
\tag{5}
\]

On every compact interval of classical existence, \(W_i\) is smooth and bounded wherever \(c_i\leq1/2\)\.

Equation (5) is a uniformly parabolic scalar equation near the face \(c_i=0\)\. Its reaction term vanishes at that face.

Standard invariant-region arguments, or approximation by strictly positive initial compositions, therefore preserve nonnegativity. Conservation of the sum preserves \(\sum_i c_i=1\)\.

Moreover, the scalar strong maximum principle gives

\[
\boxed{
\bar c_i>0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
c_i(t,x)>0
\quad\text{for all }t>0
}
\tag{6}
\]

throughout the interval on which the strong solution exists.

This is valid for arbitrary \(N\), arbitrary positive frictions, and arbitrary smooth divergence-free \(b\)\. It does not require equal, additive or multiplicative frictions.

However, the bounds on \(W_i\) involve the other species' fluxes and hence their spatial gradients. Formula (5) proves positive-time positivity; it does not give an input-only uniform lower bound on the concentrations or prevent a future gradient singularity.
